question.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Line Given in Canonical Form
question.problem: Find the parametric equations of the line $\frac{x-11}{-4}=\frac{y+3}{5}=\frac{z+1}{3}.$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that the Cartesian (canonical) equation of the straight line that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$, is given by

$$
\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\frac{x-11}{-4}=\frac{y-(-3)}{5}=\frac{z-(-1)}{3},
$$

we find that our line passes through the point $P(11,-3,-1)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨-4,5,3⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations are the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=11-4t \\ y=-3+5t \\ z=-1+3t\end{aligned}
$$
